articles.title: Genesis Championship: Yuto Katsuragawa takes two-shot lead into final day as he ties course record with flawless 63
articles.summary: Japan's Yuto Katsuragawa is 13 under at the Genesis Championship, holding a two-stroke lead going into the final day; Katsuragawa shot a flawless third-round eight-under 63 at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club; watch Sunday's final round live on Sky Sports Golf from 3am
articles.body:
Katsuragawa shot a flawless eight-under 63 in the third round at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club, including four birdies in his first five holes, to match Jinam Kang's record in 2006.

The 28-year-old is 13 under overall, two shots ahead of South Africa's Casey Jarvis.

Jarvis is seeking a third win of the 2026 season, after the Kenya Open and South African Open in February, to close in on the top three in the Race to Dubai standings - Eugenio Chacarra, Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.

Reed and McIlroy are not competing this week. Chacarra, who is No 1 in the standings after winning in India last week, was 10 shots back after the third round and tied for 30th.

There are two more events left in the European tour season, in Abu Dhabi and then Dubai.

articles.title: Cowboys Get Stunning Dak Prescott Trade Take From Skip Bayless
articles.summary: Skip Bayless has grown frustrated with the Dallas Cowboys’ uneven start and said he would immediately swap starting quarterback Dak Prescott for Washington C...
articles.body:
Skip Bayless has grown frustrated with the Dallas Cowboys' uneven start and said he would immediately swap starting quarterback Dak Prescott for Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels.

The Cowboys sit at 2-4 after six games in the 2026 season, most recently falling 23-13 to the Green Bay Packers. Prescott has drawn criticism during the stretch, including after a 24-16 home loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Bayless, a longtime Cowboys supporter, made the remarks on the Gridiron podcast alongside Aqib Talib. He pointed to the team's results with Prescott available in recent seasons.

Skip Bayless Open to Straight-Up Dak Prescott Deal for Jayden Daniels

In the clip shared by Gridiron on X, Bayless made his opinion crystal clear.

"If they want to trade me Jayden Daniels for Dak Prescott. It's done. Straight up, player for player. Let me have him, I'll take it," Bayless said .

"He was available all last year when we went 7-9-1. He's been available this year; we're 2-4. Give me Jayden Daniels."

Daniels, in his third season, has started four games for the Commanders this year. He has completed 75 of 116 passes for 759 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions, posting a 97.6 passer rating. He has also rushed for 213 yards and two scores.

Prescott has started all six games for Dallas. He is 163 of 246 for 1,639 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions with a 90.1 rating and 66.3 percent completion rate. The Cowboys rank sixth in the league in passing yards per game at 273.2 but sit near the bottom of the league in rushing.

The Cowboys face the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night in Week 7. Philadelphia is also 2-4, and a Dallas victory would move the Cowboys into a tie for second in the NFC East. The New York Giants lead the division at 3-2-1, while the Commanders are 1-4-1.

Dallas finished 7-9-1 last season with Prescott under center for most of the year. Daniels, as a rookie in 2024, helped the Commanders reach the NFC Championship Game. The Cowboys have not advanced beyond the divisional round during Prescott's tenure as the full-time starter since 2016.

Prescott's recent outings include a 34-of-54, 258-yard performance with one touchdown and two interceptions against Green Bay. Against Tampa Bay he went 24 of 42 for 316 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the loss that snapped the Buccaneers' winless streak.

The Cowboys' defense has allowed 26.5 points per game and ranks near the bottom of the league against the run. Offense has produced 25.2 points per game, but turnovers have been an issue in the losses.

Bayless has long argued that Dallas needs a different approach at quarterback after years of regular-season production without deep playoff runs.

The team remains in contention in a weak NFC East, with games remaining against Arizona, Indianapolis and others before a late-season rematch with Philadelphia.

articles.title: Booker scores 43 points in Suns' 131-122 win over Warriors, who fall to 0-3
articles.summary: PHOENIX (AP) — Devin Booker scored 43 points, Miles Bridges added 16 and the Phoenix Suns won their home opener for the fifth straight season by beating the...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Devin Booker scored 43 points, Miles Bridges added 16 and the Phoenix Suns won their home opener for the fifth straight season by beating the short-handed Golden State Warriors 131-122 on Saturday night.

The Warriors — who were playing for the third time in four days — fell to 0-3 for the first time in 19 years while resting several key players, including Stephen Curry (right knee), Brandin Podziemski (low back), Draymond Green (low back) and Al Horford (low back).

Booker scored 17 points in the third quarter and Jordan Goodwin hit a 3-pointer just before the buzzer to give the Suns a 102-92 lead entering the fourth. The Warriors hung around for a few more minutes, but the Suns eventually pulled away and Luke Kennard hit a 3 to extend the lead to 117-102 with six minutes left.

Kennard finished with 11 points, hitting 3 of 5 from 3-point range, which is exactly what the team expected when they signed him in the offseason. Dillon Brooks had 15 points and five assists.

The Suns were coming off an embarrassing 124-83 road loss in the season opener to the Trail Blazers. They struggled in the opening quarter of Saturday's game, too, making just 1 of 12 shots from 3-point range.

But the shots finally started to fall and it was Booker who led the way. The five-time All-Star made 17 of 25 from the field and added seven assists and seven rebounds.

Golden State was led by rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who scored a season-high 26 points and made six 3-pointers. De'Anthony Melton added 25 points on 8 of 13 shooting.

Booker scored 19 points in the first half, leading the Suns to a 57-54 halftime lead. Lendeborg had 13 for the Warriors.

articles.title: El japonés Katsuragawa gana en Corea con 'trastienda' española
articles.standfirst: Su entrenador de putt es Alejandro Larrazábal y su caddie Eric Shukart. Jorge Campillo acaba cuarto. Chacarra, más líder de la Race to Dubai
articles.summary: Su entrenador de putt es Alejandro Larrazábal y su caddie Eric Shukart. Jorge Campillo acaba cuarto. Chacarra, más líder de la Race to Dubai
articles.body: Yuto Katsuragawa, japonés de 28 años, se llevó el Genesis Championship en Cheonan (Corea del Sur) con solvencia. Tanto que le bastó un bogey en el hoyo 18 para firmar el par del campo (71) en la última jornada y ganar por dos golpes de diferencia. Fue un domingo con tantos nervios por ser el último torneo de la temporada regular que al campeón le valieron 16 pares y un birdie más para levantar el segundo título de su carrera en el DP World Tour. Su éxito fue también el de dos españoles: su caddie Eric Sukhart, catalán, y también de Alejandro Larrazábal, el golfista que se está ganando una reputada fama de buen entrenador de putt, tras más de una década en la docencia golfística en todas las facetas del juego. La semana pasada lo logró con Eugenio López-Chacarra y ahora con el japonés, que era una calamidad con ese palo hasta caer en sus manos. Era el 158 de la estadística de putt en el DP World Tour. (Resultados) Katsuragawa, que se jugaba aguantar la tarjeta, jugó con confianza y viendo como en los últimos nueve hoyos el resto de aspirantes claudicaba. Falló Casey Jarvis, cuarto como Jorge Campillo y otros al final, con sendos doble bogeys. Falló Ryan Fox, el campeón del Open Británico, con un bogey en el 17. Y la legión de franceses, salvo Martin Couvra (69) con un swing que enamora, pero que despachó el domingo con sólo dos birdies. Campillo se quedó a un golpe del subcampeonato, que hubiese sido el tercero del curso y el decimoquinto de su carrera. Y tiró para ello en el par 5 del hoyo 18 pero el putt se le fue a la derecha. Los 70 golpes, no obstante, con tres birdies y dos bogeys, anunciaron definitivamente su regreso después de una segunda parte de la temporada minada de problemas con el putt. En Corea, de paso, se ha asegurado la presencia en la final de Dubái. Ahí pretende llegar como líder Eugenio López-Chacarra. Cerró el torneo con un 68 que le elevó a la vigésimo segunda posición. Apenas añadió 51 puntos más en su casillero, pero ya distancia en 999 a Rory McIlroy, que parece la gran amenaza para los dos últimos torneos en el Golfo Pérsico. A Patrick Reed le tiene a 669. Todo se decidirá en los Emiratos... si las armas no trasladan su final a Sotogrande a un solo torneo. El final de la temporada regular, además, arrojó una historia de superación fabulosa. Sean Crocker en el tee del 10, con tres sobre par en esos momentos, estaba fuera de las tarjetas para el próximo curso por un puesto. Los 9 hoyos finales del estadounidense fueron de antología. Los jugó en 29 golpes, con seis birdies, cuatro en los últimos cuatro hoyos y se metió justo en el puesto 100 de la clasificación general que fija el corte. Las batallas del furgón de cola cuando el golf pasa de pelear por el espectáculo a por el empleo.

articles.title: Yuri Yoshida takes first LPGA title at BMW Ladies Championship holding off Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi in tight finish
articles.summary: Yuri Yoshida enjoyed a dramatic win to claim her first LPGA title; Yoshida won the LPGA South Korea tournament, holding off Haeran Ryu and Hye-Jin Choi in a close finish; both Ryu and Yoshida bogeyed the final hole, leaving the Japanese player ahead by one stoke at 17-under
articles.body:
It was Yoshida's first LPGA Tour victory and came in a dramatic finale as both overnight leader Ryu and Yoshida bogeyed the final hole, leaving the Japanese player ahead by one stroke at 17-under after four rounds.

Yoshida was four shots off the pace going into Sunday's final round but lit up the front nine with an eagle at the par-five second, followed by three consecutive birdies.

Bogeys at the 15th and 18th were offset by a crucial birdie at the 17th, which gave the 26-year-old the buffer she needed.

Ryu led the tournament by four strokes going into the final round but could not find the same rhythm on Sunday as she shot a 73 to finish at 16 under.

The South Korean made 15 consecutive pars before dropping a crucial shot at the par-four 16th, which handed back Yoshida's one-shot advantage.

Both players made birdies at the 17th but a costly miss for Ryu at 18 allowed Yoshida to clinch it, despite the Japanese golfer also making bogey.

Hye-Jin Choi, who was in a tie for second coming into the final round, stayed in contention throughout Sunday and mixed four birdies with a lone bogey to finish at 16 under - a shot behind Yoshida and in a tie for second with Ryu.

Choi is still looking for her first victory in 125 career LPGA Tour starts as a member. She has held or shared a 54-hole lead five times without converting it into a win.

Last week in Shanghai, Choi was runner-up by one stroke to China's Ruoning Yin after the South Korean golfer led after each of the first three rounds.

Defending champion Sei Young Kim, who ended a five-year victory drought in 2025 with a win last year in South Korea, shot 70 on Sunday and finished at two under and in a tie for 55th.

In its late-season Asian swing, the LPGA Tour moves to Kuala Lumpur next week for the Maybank Championship, the third of four events.

articles.title: Genesis Championship: Yuto Katsuragawa secures victory finishing two shots ahead of Frederic Lacroix and Martin Couvra
articles.summary: Yuto Katsuragawa finished two shots ahead of Frederic Lacroix and Martin Couvra to win the Genesis Championship; a day after equalling the course record at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club, Katsuragawa held on to his lead to win his second DP World Tour title
articles.body:
A day after scoring a flawless eight-under 63 in the third round to tie the course record at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club, the Japanese player - who won his first title more than two years ago at the ISPS Handa Championship in Japan - shot a more circumspect even-par 71 in the final round as he maintained his comfortable advantage in the final holes, despite a tap-in bogey at the last.

After four rounds, 28-year-old Katsuragawa was 13 under, two shots ahead of French pair Frederic Lacroix (68) and Martin Couvra (69).

Japan's Katsuragawa entered the week in 106th place on the Race to Dubai Rankings, fighting to keep his playing privileges for the 2027 season. This has catapulted him to 28th and guaranteed his spot in the two Rolex Series events in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

South Africa's Casey Jarvis (72), who was in second place going into Sunday's championship round, fell back into a tie for fourth with seven other players, including Open champion Ryan Fox (70) at 10 under.

Jarvis was seeking a third win of the 2026 season, after the Kenya Open and South African Open in February, to close in on the top three in the Race to Dubai standings - Eugenio Chacarra, Patrick Reed and Rory McIlroy.

Reed and McIlroy did not compete this week. Chacarra, who is No 1 in the standings after winning in India last week, finished seven shots back at six under, tied for 22nd.

There are two more events left in the European tour season, in Abu Dhabi and then Dubai.

Katsuragawa said: "After the first win, I had such a hard time, struggling with that time, but having the second win, this is definitely the greatest moment of my life.

"I was nervous, not just for the victory but also about the seed for the DP World Tour so it was double nervous for me, but I think I got through.

"I had a good image from the first victory, I just kept that good feeling about it and I came for the second win.

"I'm very happy because to play on the DP World Tour is something I need in my life and I am very happy to play in Dubai."

articles.title: Pornanong Phatlum wins Hero Women's Indian Open for the fourth time as she overhauls home favourite Vani Kapoor
articles.summary: Pornanong Phatlum overtook Vani Kapoor on the latter's home course to win the 2026 Hero Women's Indian Open for a fourth time; "Every putt on the front nine dropped in the hole. Today feels incredible," she said
articles.body:
Phatlum went bogey-free in the final round at DLF Golf & Country Club to leapfrog home favourite Vani Kapoor and secure a four-shot victory on 11 under par.

"I'm so happy right now," said the 36-year-old, who also won the trophy on the Arnold Palmer course in 2008, 2009 and 2012.

"I didn't think I was going to win again, but I tried my best. This was a fantastic round for me. Every putt on the front nine dropped in the hole. Today feels incredible.

"I wanted to come back and try my best here again because I have such good memories here - wonderful memories. This is my fourth win here, so it makes me very happy."

Teeing up in the final group with Kapoor and defending champion Shannon Tan on Sunday, and trailing the Indian by one shot, a match play situation quickly ensued between the two as both players birdied the opening par-4 - Kapoor after chipping in from the back of the green.

The home favourite would birdie the second to open up a two shot lead before Phatlum responded with a fine birdie at the third. This was followed by three more birdies at the fifth, eighth and ninth as the Sunday rivals made the turn all square.

On to the back nine, and Kapoor would squander her lead for the first time in the final round, dropping a stroke at the 10th after her tee shot took at unfortunate kick.

Despite a bounce-back birdie at the 11th, Kapoor handed LPGA star Phatlum the advantage again by dropping shots at the 12th and 13th.

After a string of pars, birdies followed at the 15th and 16th as Phatlum drained two brilliant putts. Two pars to finish in front of the watching gallery would secure Phatlum a four-shot victory and historic fourth title - 18 years after her first.

Playing at her home course, DLF Golf & Country Club Kapoor came second on seven under, still her best finish on the LET.

"I gave it my best," said Kapoor, who carded a round of 70 (-2) on Sunday. "Everything went according to plan. I don't think I could have done anything more. I made a lot of birdies, especially considering the amount of pressure there was.

"I don't think I would have made so many birdies in a single round before. I made a couple of mistakes too, but that's part of the game. It's better to accept it."

articles.title: Laura Frick named 2029 Ryder Cup championship director at Hazeltine National
articles.summary: Laura Frick makes history again as she is named the championship director for the 2029 Ryder Cup at Hazeltine National.
articles.body:
Laura Frick made history earlier this year as the first female PGA of America Golf Professional to serve as championship director for one of the association's spectator championships, holding the role at the 2026 KPMG Women's PGA Championship at Hazeltine National in Chaska, Minnesota.

Now, she's stepping into an even bigger role for one of the biggest events in golf: championship director of the 2029 Ryder Cup .

The PGA of America announced Sunday that Frick would assume the role for the next U.S. edition of the biennial bash, which returns to Hazeltine National, where the Ryder Cup was also held in 2016. And Frick, who was introduced to the game by her grandparents as an 8-year-old in Hudsonville, Michigan, will have a front-row seat to all on-site operations for the Ryder Cup.

"It's truly a job that I will look forward to waking up for every day," Frick said. "I'm proud of the dedication it took to get here and I'm so thankful for the network of people who guided and supported me along the way."

After graduating from Ferris State in 2015, Frick joined the PGA of America and worked in the Player Engagement and Member Championships departments. In December 2021, she became Director of Competitions, leading national events that included the PGA Jr. League Championships.

Now, her newest role will be in the same place she made history at this summer.

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

articles.title: Women's India Open: Vani Kapoor makes herself heard but Phatlum has last word
articles.summary: GURUGRAM: The autumn leaves were falling on the vantage point, where many had gathered for a glimpse of the ninth hole at DLF G&CC.
articles.body: GURUGRAM: The autumn leaves were falling on the vantage point, where many had gathered for a glimpse of the ninth hole at DLF G&CC. Overnight leader Vani Kapoor’s rousing birdie on the eighth kept her one ahead of the experienced Thai, Pornanong Phatlum, already a three-time winner at the venue, although on the old Arnold Palmer-designed layout.People could sense a turning point as the LPGA golfer collected her fifth birdie of the day. The home pro stood over her small pressure putt, studying the lines over and over again, taking a step backwards, playing it in her mind, then attempting again. Finally she hit, it was a miss!A leaf fell again on the shoulder. Was it nature’s way of saying that the hopes had withered too? The spectators remained still, in disbelief, then politely clapped in admiration as the calm Thai caught up with the home challenger.Maybe that elusive Hero Women’s Indian Open trophy had slipped out of our hands again.Onto the par-4 10th, and Vani’s second shot was short, and her wedge failed to find the right spot on the green. As Phatlum settled for her two-putt par, Vani's putter missed the target again for a bogey. The narrative had changed.This is the club where Vani, a star student of the DLF Academy, had grown up. A casual walk here would often lead to one bumping into the little confident girl whose dreams were big. Older now at 32, her expectations were now tempered with a sprinkling of reality. But despite all the disappointments home and away, she carried on with a happy demeanour.In golf, you could be second but you were still a winner but only one could walk away with the prize, and that person needed a little bit of luck, she had said before.The stumbles on the back-nine ensured that Vani came second. Yes, she was still a winner. But champion Phatlum made her own luck. When the Indian came out, all irons blazing, with four birdies in five holes, the Thai managed three of her own, adding two more before the turn.Pars can be powerful if you are ahead, and others are not making their moves. Phatlum was creating her own new chapter with two more birdies after the lull under the strong afternoon sun for a final-day bogey-free seven-under 65, and a magical fourth triumph by four strokes.Vani quietly accepted her lot with her round of 70, as her bogey tumbles on the return journey set the tone for the unhappy conclusion. “I think this year I was much more confident, and more anchored. I had much more clarity in my head and a sense of purpose,” she shared her positive notes.But she had felt the pressure. “Some shots you don’t have exactly have the yardage you want, and you have to think about where you can miss the ball. Those are stressful, so there were little mistakes there.”But where the margins are minute, especially on the slopey greens of the Gary Player course, little could become large when you are fighting for the championship. “I don’t think I could have done anything more. I made a lot of birdies, especially considering the amount of pressure there was. I made a couple of mistakes too, but that’s part of the game.”Golf can be cruel, it can also be rejuvenating.For the petite Thai conqueror with an infectious smile, this is the end of a long drought.Phatlum, who has returned to India after 14 years on an invite, had her first look at the changed environment and used all her experience on American shores to plot her way around the course where “every shot counts”.With soft skills to match the Mudmee silk her hometown of Khon Kaen is famous for, Phatlum steadily improved with rounds of 72, 71, 69 as her understanding of the playground grew, to finish on a high of 65. With a solo second at the 2018 Women’s British Open in her resume, the Women’s Indian Open champion of 2008, 2009 and 2012 had seen better years on the LPGA. With the 2026 crown, her love affair with the tournament continued. “I think I could live in India,” the 36-year-old said, giggling.Stomach bug Pranavi's biggest challengeThe Indians are getting closer to that hallowed trophy, which Aditi Ashok won in 2016.A second place finish is as good as it gets for now. “It was Pornanong’s experience which came clutch today,” explained Pranavi Urs, who finished tied-fourth.It was a week the Asian Games gold medallist was looking forward to. “With the way I’ve been playing, I thought I would have a chance.”The biggest obstacle was not the course, but her stomach. Not having a proper meal since Pro-Am day, the breathless figure could be seen struggling as the day progressed. Despite the trouble, the Mysuru girl finished with a 72 and a total of three-under.Tvesa Malik was the third Indian in the top-10, at 7th place.Final scores: -11 Pornanong Phatlum (Tha) 72-71-69-65; -7 Vani Kapoor (Ind) 73-69-69-70; -4 Shannon Tan (Sin) 68-77-67-72; -3 Sara Kouskova (Cze) 70-70-73-72; Pranavi Urs (Ind) 70-70-73-72; Select scores: -1 (7th) Tvesa Malik 71-73-71-72; +2 (T9) Chiara Tamburlini (Sui); +6 (22) Avani Prashanth.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Board of Deputies of British Jews declares Greens to be racist party
articles.summary: The Jewish body's vote comes in response to the Green Party passing a "Zionism is racism" policy motion.
articles.body:
The Green Party of England and Wales has been declared a racist organisation by the Board of Deputies of British Jews.

The Jewish body, which is the largest in the UK, was responding to the "Zionism is racism" policy motion passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.

Board of Deputies president Phil Rosenberg said a vote passed by 118 votes to one to declare that the Greens had, "by adopting an antisemitic platform, become a racist party".

A spokesman for the Greens insisted the party does not discriminate against people who hold Zionist views and said it rejected the Board of Deputies' "characterisation of this motion and our party".

They added the decision "will not stop us from speaking out against the genocide in Gaza and pushing for stronger sanctions against the Israeli government and its leaders". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

The motion passed by the Board of Deputies urged other parties not to do deals with the Greens unless they rejected the policy.

Forming coalition deals with Greens at local or national level would be "failing to take antisemitism with the requisite seriousness", it said, unless the party's local leadership have rejected the policy and committed to overturn it.

Labour has already issued an ultimatum to local Green groups it is currently in coalition with, telling them to disown the motion or lose the party's support.

Rosenberg said: "By adopting an antisemitic platform, the Green Party of England and Wales has become a racist party. We will treat it accordingly.

"No political party has the right to tell Jews that a central part of our identity, rooted in thousands of years of history, faith and peoplehood, is racist.

"The Green Party's policy brands much of our community, including our synagogues and communal organisations, with that slur. It gives prejudice against Jews a political licence.

"The Green Party's leadership must now take responsibility for reversing this policy and confronting the antisemitism it has legitimised."

The motion backed by Green members at its party conference earlier this month said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/ or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It was criticised by Jewish groups, as well as four Green MPs and two former leaders, and opposition political parties.

Responding when the Green motion was passed, the Board of Deputies and Jewish Leadership Council said in a joint statement that "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it".

Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, did not take part in the vote on the motion as he left the conference early to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election which was held days later.

He has since told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, he would not overturn the motion , which would be party policy until 2028.

articles.title: El final del LIV Golf: Quiebra, deudas... y bonus millonarios a los directivos
articles.standfirst: Jugadores y proveedores siguen manteniendo deudas
articles.summary: Jugadores y proveedores siguen manteniendo deudas
articles.body: El primero fulgurante y después polémico LIV Golf -el circuito multimillonario financiado principalmente por el fondo nacional de inversión de Arabia Saudí- está teniendo un final polémico. A la espera de saber si el circuito se recicla en una versión 2.0, una información del prestigioso medio especializado Golf Digest añade un significativo detalle sobre el modelo de gestión: LIV Golf pagó a los ejecutivos 15,6 millones de dólares en bonos, poco antes de la declaración de bancarrota, mientras los proveedores seguían a la espera de pago por sus servicios. Es decir, uno de los modelos de gestión empresarial más criticados: empresas en crisis que siguen pagando generosamente a los directivos que la han llevado a ella. El pago más grande, según la información fue para el CEO Scott O'Neil, a quien se atribuye un bono de 6,375 millones de dólares el 24 de junio, menos de tres meses antes de la declaración de bancarrota del circuito. Solo unos meses antes, O'Neil recibió otro bono de alrededor de $ 2,7 millones. En total desde el pasado mes de septiembre se le pagaron más de 13,6 millones en nómina, bonos, beneficios, pagos de retención y reembolsos de gastos, según los registros. Además, el director financiero, David Phillips, recibió más de 3,3 millones, y el director legal John Ruzich, alrededor de 2,6 millones. Greg Norman, predecesor de O'Neil y comisionado fundador de LIV, recibió más de 9,4 millones cuando dejó la liga en septiembre de 2025. No fueron los únicos beneficiarios. Mientras tanto, según Golf Digest, LIV no pagó a contratistas y proveedores. El pasado septiembre, LIV Golf despidió a la mayoría de su personal. Los jugadores se encuentran entre los mayores acreedores. El LIV Golf podría encontrar una vía de reestructuración por medio de un acuerdo con la compañía financiera BC Partners Credit, que anunció que aportará una inversión de 300 millones de dólares (unos 265 millones de euros) para el nuevo proyecto LIV 2.0. Una cifra muy lejana a las cantidades aportadas por los saudíes. De momento el calendario se reduciría a 10 torneos, con menos premios.

articles.title: Bermuda Championship: Seamus Power set for Monday play-off against Austin Smotherman as final round is scrapped due to bad weather
articles.summary: The Butterfield Bermuda Championship was reduced to 54 holes after bad weather forced PGA Tour organisers to cancel the final round; co-leaders Seamus Power and Austin Smotherman will go head-to-head in a play-off on Monday
articles.body:
The PGA Tour confirmed the news on Sunday evening, with Power and Smotherman leading on 16 under heading into the final round, two shots clear of a chasing pack that included Taylor Moore, Corey Conners and Ben Silverman.

PGA Tour referees had been assessing the possibility of hosting the final round on Monday, but with forecasts predicting more rain and heavy winds, officials confirmed the tournament would be ended prematurely.

However, Power and Smotherman's play-off is scheduled for 12pm (GMT), weather permitting.

It marks the first time in two years that a PGA Tour event has been forced to conclude after 54 holes after Wyndham Clark sealed victory at the weather-affected 2024 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am.

"Due to the unfavourable weather forecast for Monday at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship and the uncertainty surrounding the completion of the entire final round on Monday, the tournament results will be considered final through 54 holes in accordance with PGA Tour Regulations," a statement from the PGA Tour read.

"A play-off between Seamus Power and Austin Smotherman will be conducted to determine the champion and is tentatively scheduled for 9am local time on Monday, subject to weather conditions."

Power, who is out to win his third PGA Tour title, notably clinched his first victory on the US circuit via a play-off, defeating JT Poston at the 2021 ISCO Championship.

Smotherman will participate in his first play-off on the PGA Tour, and is out to win his second title after claiming victory in his most recent start at the Bank of Utah Championship.

After carding opening rounds of 65 and 66, Smotherman rose seven places up the leaderboard on Saturday with another five-under 66, which included three birdies on his first five holes, and an eagle on the seventh, before going level through his back nine.

Power surged to go one shot back of the 36-hole lead after an impressive second-round 64. As many players fell away in the trying conditions, the Irishman carded an impressive four-under 67 to take a share of the lead with Smotherman through 54 holes.

Weather forecasts expect a 60 per cent chance of rain on Monday morning, as well as winds between 15 to 20mph.

articles.title: Dan Campbell Explains Controversial Fourth-Down Decision That Nearly Cost Lions vs. Packers
articles.summary: Dan Campbell explains his controversial fourth-down decision that nearly cost the Detroit Lions their 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions escaped Ford Field with a thrilling 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, but head coach Dan Campbell nearly watched one of his trademark aggressive decisions turn a huge NFC North win into a devastating loss. With the game tied late in the fourth quarter, Campbell elected to go for it on fourth-and-1 from Detroit's own 22-yard line, a decision that immediately backfired.

Rather than punt the football and trust a defense that had played exceptionally well throughout the afternoon, Campbell kept his offense on the field. Jahmyr Gibbs was stuffed for a two-yard loss, handing Green Bay possession deep in Lions territory with less than five minutes remaining.

Dan Campbell Explains His Risky Fourth-Down Decision

Following the victory, Campbell was asked why he decided to take such an enormous gamble with the game hanging in the balance. His explanation was simple, and it reflected the confidence he had in both his offense and defense.

"I thought we would get it," Campbell said following Detroit's win. "Two, I thought we would get the ball back if it didn't work out."

The decision was especially surprising considering how well Detroit's defense had performed against Jordan Love and the Packers offense. Green Bay managed just 60 rushing yards, and the Lions had already forced several important stops throughout the game.

Campbell's confidence in his defense ultimately proved justified, although the Packers came dangerously close to taking the lead. After taking over in Detroit territory, Green Bay moved into position for a 35-yard field goal, but D.J. Wonnum got a hand on Trey Smack's attempt to keep the game tied.

The failed fourth-down conversion could have been the defining moment of Detroit's afternoon, but the defense refused to let it happen. Green Bay's missed opportunity gave Jared Goff and the Lions offense another possession, and this time they delivered when it mattered most.

Goff guided Detroit down the field before Jake Bates connected on a 22-yard field goal as time expired. The victory improved the Lions to 4-2 while dropping the Packers to 4-3, giving Detroit an important win over its division rival.

Detroit finished with 415 total yards, including 303 passing yards and two touchdowns from Goff. As we previously reported , Jameson Williams delivered a spectacular opening-drive touchdown and finished the game with five receptions for 91 yards and two scores.

The Lions also received a huge performance from Amon-Ra St. Brown , who caught nine passes for 153 yards. Meanwhile, Gibbs rushed for 116 yards on 29 carries despite being stopped on the crucial fourth-down attempt.

Campbell's Aggressiveness Remains a Double-Edged Sword

Campbell has never been afraid to gamble on fourth down, and that mentality has become part of Detroit's identity during his tenure. However, going for it deep in his own territory with the score tied and less than five minutes remaining was the kind of decision that could have overshadowed everything the Lions accomplished Sunday.

Detroit finished 0-for-2 on fourth-down attempts while Green Bay converted three of its four opportunities. The Lions nevertheless found a way to survive, thanks largely to a defense that limited the Packers to 324 total yards and came through when Campbell needed it most.

The final result was another reminder that Campbell's aggressive approach can create both tremendous opportunities and unnecessary risks. This time, the Lions had enough defense, resilience, and a little good fortune to make sure his most controversial decision didn't cost them the game.

articles.title: 5 takeaways from Lions’ victory against Packers
articles.summary: 5 takeaways from the Detroit Lions’ thrilling win against the Green Bay Packers, 20-17.
articles.body:
Coming off a bye week, the Detroit Lions got extra time to prepare for the Green Bay Packers in their first NFC North battle of 2026. This game was much closer than it should've been, as Detroit dominated and its own mistakes gave Green Bay life. It came down to a game-winning kick by kicker Jake Bates, with Detroit winning 20-17.

Here are my five takeaways from the Lions' thrilling win against the Packers.

When the offense was consistent, it was dominant

Despite scoring only 20 points, the Lions offense was great when it clicked. They had an opening-drive touchdown for the first time this season, moving the ball downfield with ease as they scored in under four minutes on six plays to take the lead. Quarterback Jared Goff was wheeling and dealing, going 22-for-32 for 303 yards and two touchdowns.

Wide receiver Jameson Williams found the end zone for Detroit, catching five for 91 yards and two touchdowns. Lions' leading receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had his biggest game of the season, getting nine catches for 153 yards. The passing attack was lethal and picked apart the Packers' secondary, which relies on its safeties to bail it out. Play action worked with ease, given Green Bay's lack of depth at linebacker.

Running back Jahmyr Gibbs had highs and lows, finishing with 29 carries for 116 yards and five catches for 27 yards. His second-quarter fumble was costly, as it killed Detroit's chance to at least take a six-point lead at the half after they got the ball back. In the end, Gibbs clutched up and helped set Bates up for the game-winning kick.

The return of Brian Branch and Cade Mays was felt

Two big pieces returned for the Lions on Sunday: safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays. Mays started at center, and the offensive line struck consistently in the passing game as play-action gave Goff time to let it rip. The running game showed flashes of success. Mays did make a mistake, though, and bumped into Gibbs on the first fumble of the game.

Branch wasn't on the field as often as Mays, as his Achilles injury will take time to adjust to playing again. Despite getting limited snaps, Branch had an impact with four tackles and a huge interception in the fourth quarter. The secondary did improve with Branch back, and Mays gave the offensive line a nice boost. These two players had a big impact in the win, and the team feels like it has a better identity on offense and defense.

Detroit's defense has improved in its past two games, but its biggest problem this week was stopping the Packers on crucial downs. Green Bay was three-for-four on fourth-down attempts, getting 77 yards on those successful plays. On third-down, gotta-have-it stops, the Lions let the Packers go five-for-15.

While that isn't a high success rate, Green Bay converted on those downs and turned it into points almost every time.

Opening drive – Converted fourth down, set up a field goal that was missed

Second drive – Converted two third downs and one fourth down; result was a touchdown

Fourth drive – Converted one third and one fourth down; was stopped on downs on the lone failed fourth-down attempt

Fifth drive – One rushing play before halftime

Sixth drive – Scored touchdown pass on third down pass

Eighth drive – Interception on third down

Ninth drive – Converted one third down, made field goal

10th drive – Missed field goal on four-play drive

Detroit got bailed out by Packers kicker Trey Smack, who missed two field goals. If he'd made the first field goal, Green Bay might have kicked it on that fourth drive instead of going for it. Green Bay punted only twice all game, and if Detroit makes more stops, those punt numbers could rise.

One issue Detroit has had this season is the number of penalties they've gotten in every game. From false starts to holding on either side of the ball, Detroit has been beating itself up in some games this season. On Sunday, Detroit got called for five penalties, a slight improvement from their average of seven per game, according to TeamRankings.com.

Two were on special teams, one was a questionable penalty on linebacker Derrick Barnes, and the other two were false starts by the offensive line. The two offensive penalties didn't hurt the team or stall the drive, which was good to see compared to earlier this year. Unfortunately, when they fix one problem, another one appears.

While Detroit wasn't beating themselves with penalties, they beat themselves up with fumbles. While the Gibbs fumble was friendly fire, it still made the game closer than it was. If Gibbs hadn't fumbled it there, Detroit could have gone up by six to 10 at halftime. Detroit was moving the ball down the field with ease, and it killed the momentum.

The second turnover was another awkward play by Mays and Goff; Mays hiked it, and I don't know what happened. I don't know if Goff didn't grasp the ball or Mays snapped it too early, but it was kicked forward, and Green Bay got the ball to start both halves pretty much. While the first fumble didn't give Green Bay points, the Packers capitalized on the second fumble and scored. Those two fumbles were big swings, and they almost turned this victory into a defeat.

Detroit has to clean up the fumbles, and Goff threw multiple risky passes that should have been picked off; one was eliminated due to defensive pass interference on Green Bay. It was scary after the offense started strong, but if they can play clean football and avoid penalties and turnovers, this offense can stay one of the best in the NFL.

articles.title: Bermuda Championship: Ireland's Seamus Power misses out in Monday finish as Austin Smotherman claims PGA Tour play-off win
articles.summary: Austin Smotherman defeated Seamus Power on the third play-off hole to claim a second PGA Tour title in as many starts; Bermuda Championship was turned into a 54-hole tournament after Sunday's play was postponed due to strong winds
articles.body:
Smotherman and Power held a share of the 54-hole lead at Port Royal Golf Course, where Sunday's play was postponed due to strong winds before the final round was cancelled due to more poor weather.

It left both players tied on 16 under and returning on Monday morning for a sudden-death play-off, with both players making par - in breezy conditions - on the first two extra holes on the par-three 16th.

The hole location was changed ahead of the next extra hole, where a Power bogey meant a two-putt par was enough for Smotherman to close out victory and add to his Bank of Utah Championship title earlier this month.

" We're out here playing an incredible sport in a beautiful spot," Smotherman said after his win. "Whatever things are going to be thrown at us, Zak [Williamson, caddie] and I were going to be on top of our game.

"Yesterday [Sunday] I felt like we handled everything pretty well and the tour has been great, communicating what's going to happen today for us. Once we got that news, it was nice to know what's going on. To come out on top is a cherry on top of that, so pretty awesome."

How Smotherman edged out Power in Bermuda

Smotherman had followed an opening-round 65 with successive 66s over the next two days to move into a share of the lead, with Power posting a four-under 67 on Saturday to also get to 16 under.

The PGA Tour said on Sunday evening that, due to an 'unfavourable weather forecast and uncertainty surrounding the completion of the entire final round', the tournament would be declared as a 54-hole event.

The play-off was played on loop on the 178-yard 16th on Monday morning, where Smotherman produced a good up and down from right of the green to match Power's two-putt par on the first extra hole.

Power splashed out of the sand to five feet and made his par on the second, where Smotherman found the green and two-putted from distance, with the pin location changed and the yardage cut to 152 yards before they faced the hole for a third time.

Momentum moved Smotherman's way when Power sent his iron into the left rough and then barely advanced his ball onto the green with his second, leading to a bogey as Smotherman two-putted from 15 feet to add another victory.

Smotherman becomes the eighth multiple winner this season and first to win successive PGA Tour events since Matt Fitzpatrick, while the 54-hole tournament is the first on the PGA Tour since the 2024 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am.

The PGA Tour heads to Mexico for the VidantaWorld Mexico Championship, beginning Thursday at Vidanta Vallarta and where Brian Campbell returns as defending champion.

articles.title: Bermuda Championship: Austin Smotherman beats Seamus Power in Monday play-off for second PGA Tour win
articles.summary: Austin Smotherman claims his second PGA Tour title with a Monday play-off victory over Seamus Power at the weather-hit Bermuda Championship.
articles.body:
Austin Smotherman claimed his second PGA Tour title with a Monday play-off victory over Seamus Power at the weather-hit Bermuda Championship.

The 32-year-old American parred the third extra hole to fend off the Irishman and seal his second tournament win in as many starts after a breakthrough victory in Utah earlier this month.

Smotherman and Power contested the sudden-death play-off on Monday after inclement weather forced organisers to cancel Sunday's scheduled final round.

With more bad weather forecast on Monday, officials decided to scrap the final round and proceed with a play-off between the 54-hole leaders.

Smotherman carded 65, 66 and 66 to reach 16 under through three rounds, with 2022 champion Power matching his 197 total with rounds of 66, 64 and 67.

On the first play-off hole - the par-three 16th at Port Royal Golf Course - Power missed a 20-footer for his third PGA Tour win before getting up and down from the bunker to force a third extra hole.

With the hole location having been changed, Smotherman two-putted from 15 feet for the win after Power failed to get up and down for par from the rough.

"We're out here playing an incredible sport in a beautiful spot," said Smotherman.

"Whatever things are going to be thrown at us, Zak [Williamson, caddie] and I were going to be on top of our game.

"Yesterday I felt like we handled everything pretty well and the tour has been great at communicating what's going to happen today for us.

"Once we got that news, it was nice to know what's going on. To come out on top is a cherry on top, so it's pretty awesome."

While Power missed out on the trophy, the runner-up finish effectively guarantees his PGA Tour card for 2027 after playing with conditional status this year.

Having entered the week 103rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, the 39-year-old is projected to climb to 53rd, with the top 100 earning PGA Tour cards for next year.

"Had a chance this morning, wasn't able to do it, which is disappointing, but overall great week, can't complain too much," said Power.

"Hit some good shots in the playoff, just didn't quite judge the wind right, but that's golf sometimes. I'll move onwards."

articles.title: Cam Young was out the door to LIV Golf, wind cuts PGA Tour event short, and gearing up for Mexico
articles.summary: PGA Tour star Cameron Young signed a document of intent to join LIV Golf after the 2022 Open Championship, newly revealed bankruptcy filings show.
articles.body: The PGA Tour returned this week, kind of, which means Par Talk is also back to its regularly scheduled programming as we gear up for four straight weeks of action to close out the Fall Swing. The Butterfield Bermuda Championship is sneakily one of the most entertaining events of the fall, with players competing for status on an island in some of the windiest conditions they'll ever play in. Unfortunately, the PGA Tour deemed the wind on Sunday and Monday to be too much and cut the event to 54 holes. There were eight players within three shots of the lead heading into the final round, but ultimately, the Tour let 54-hole co-leaders Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power duel it out in a Monday playoff at Port Royal. As for the biggest news out of the golf world from the past week, it involves bankruptcy, Cameron Young, and his signature on an agreement to join LIV Golf years ago. Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com. Cameron Young was out the door to LIV Golf Cameron Young was open about having interest in potentially joining LIV Golf during its inaugural season in 2022. The American openly stated at that year's Tour Championship in Atlanta that he was interested in making the jump to the then Saudi-backed circuit. Recently revealed court documents revealed that Young's interest in a move wasn't just a thought he was tossing around in his brain, but one he took legitimate action on. JON RAHM WON'T PARTICIPATE UNDER LIV GOLF'S 'UNACCEPTABLE' NEW TERMS AMID LEAGUE'S BANKRUPTCY, LAWYERS SAY As LIV Golf is going through proceedings after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, documents revealed that the circuit paid $15.6 million in retention payments to executives before filing. Not lost in the shuffle, which showed that LIV CEO Scott O'Neil received a retention of more than $6 million, was Young previously signing a document of intent to join LIV following the 2022 Open Championship at St. Andrews. The 2022 Open Championship, while a classic finish with Cameron Smith edging out Rory McIlroy, was already remembered as 'The One With The LIV Distraction,' but even more so now. Smith joined LIV shortly after hoisting the Claret Jug, and with Young signing his intent dated July 24, one week after the final round, he was ready to follow suit. The speculation about Young jumping ship from the PGA Tour continued to gain steam for another four weeks before he ultimately grew tired of the questions and shared he had decided to stay on the Tour following the final round of the 2022 Tour Championship. Young was ranked 17th in the world at the time with zero wins on Tour to his name. Since then, he's moved up to No. 4 in the world, won three times, including the 2026 Players, and has represented the United States at both the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup. Austin Smotherman gets it done in Bermuda The PGA Tour was scrambling on Monday. Pun absolutely intended. articles.title: Packers Fans Want Trey Smack Cut After Lions Loss
articles.summary: Packers fans want their kicker gone after two short misses at Ford Field. #OnePride
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack left two short field goals on the floor at Ford Field on Sunday, and plenty of Packers fans want him off the roster. Head coach Matt LaFleur does not.

After the 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said, "Certainly you never want to go through it, but Trey's a guy, I think he's proven that he can do it. I know he can do it. But we've got to wipe this one clean and move on." It appears as if LaFleur is sticking with Smack as his kicker moving forward despite the struggles.

How Trey Smack's Day Unraveled in Detroit

Smack pushed a 26-yard attempt wide right in the first quarter, a kick that a delay of game penalty had backed up from 21 yards . He tied the game at 17 with a 43-yarder in the fourth quarter, then had a 35-yard try blocked by Lions defender DJ Wonnum with 3:25 to play. Detroit took the ball back and Jake Bates ended it with a 22-yard walk-off field goal. The Lions improved to 4-2 on the season, and the Packers dropped to 4-3.

Green Bay Packers Fans Call for Trey Smack to Be Cut

There are a lot of Green Bay fans who are not happy with LaFleur sticking with Smack. A lot of fans believe that Smack was the reason why they lost against the Lions. The kicker was not the only target of Packers frustration after the game, either: safety Xavier McKinney unloaded on the officiating crew .

Smack is 11 of 16 on field goals this season and 13 of 15 on extra points. Pro Football Talk put it bluntly : "NFL kickers are 167-for-170 from inside 37 yards. Trey Smack had 2 of the 3 misses Sunday." The Packers do not have much time to sort it out, either. They are back at Lambeau Field on Thursday, Oct. 29 against the Carolina Panthers.

articles.title: LIV Golf: Former US Open champion Graeme McDowell confirms exit
articles.summary: Northern Ireland's Graeme McDowell becomes the latest major champion to exit LIV Golf.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland's Graeme McDowell has become the latest major champion to confirm his departure from LIV Golf.

The 2010 US Open winner, 47, announced on Monday he has "decided not to pursue" LIV 2.0, the new version of the breakaway tour which is due to start in 2027.

Major winners Jon Rahm and Louis Oosthuizen have also confirmed their departures, while McDowell's fellow countryman Tom McKibbin said he was exiting LIV to return to the DP World Tour last week.

England's Tyrrell Hatton and Ian Poulter have also left the competition.

Saudi's Public Investment Fund withdrew its backing from LIV in April - having pumped in more than $5bn (£3.8bn) - leading to the league filing for bankruptcy protection in the United States last month.

It has secured a possible $300m (£224m) in financing from BC Partners Credit to try to move forward with 'LIV 2.0', but only a handful of players have so far committed.

Former world number four McDowell joined LIV when it launched as a lucrative Saudi Arabia-backed project in 2022.

The 11-time DP World Tour winner's best finish on LIV was a tie for second in Virginia in June 2025.

"I've decided not to pursue LIV 2.0," said four-time Ryder Cup player McDowell.

"I'm grateful for the opportunity I've had over the last four years and want to thank everyone who has been part of that journey.

"I look forward to the next chapter in my career."

Earlier this year, McDowell told BBC Sport NI he had held "really positive" talks about returning to the DP World Tour next season, adding he was "lucky to have that option".

Poulter & Hatton leave LIV as exodus continues

Rahm sacrifices £75m to secure exit from LIV Golf

Former Open champion Oosthuizen quits LIV Golf

LIV pushes on by appointing new senior adviser

Meanwhile, LIV has announced the appointment of former Taylor Made and Adidas executive Mark King as senior adviser.

King said: "Having spent much of my career in golf, I believe there is a tremendous opportunity for LIV Golf to establish itself as a competitive and enduring force in the game."

In the same announcement, the league said it "remains laser focused on advancing its conversations with players regarding their participation" in LIV 2.0.

A deadline for player sign-ups had been set for Sunday, although BBC Sport understands there is a degree of flexibility to enable ongoing discussions with players.

The lawyer representing LIV told a bankruptcy court hearing earlier this month it needed to sign a "sufficient number of players to have a bona fide golf league", and would know by the end of October whether it could proceed with LIV 2.0 or move to winding down the breakaway league.

League sources told BBC Sport that LIV 2.0 is generating "inbound interest from established, elite professionals and emerging talent across global professional golf".

articles.title: Renfrew flooded after council failed to activate barriers during Storm Boelo
articles.summary: Renfrewshire Council said "predicted tide levels" for the storm did not meet the threshold needed to use the flood barriers.
articles.body:
A crucial part of a flood defence system that cost millions of pounds to install in Renfrew was not activated by a council ahead of Storm Boelo, despite an amber weather warning.

Renfrewshire Council said "predicted tide levels and available forecast data" for the storm did not meet the threshold needed to use flood barriers.

Water from the River Clyde burst through on Saturday night and swamped shops and homes in the area, causing serious damage to local businesses.

The North Renfrew Flood Prevention Scheme cost about £10m to install. When it was launched in 2016, officials declared it would provide protection against any extreme flooding events.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

The flood prevention scheme includes both a three-metre high embankment and an underground pumping station.

However, while the pumping station was in use, the council said its data - which included predicted tide levels for the Clyde - did not reach a required threshold for using the barriers.

It said water levels on Saturday then rose far higher than had been predicted.

Locals described being being knee deep in the water as it surged through.

Maureen Gray works in the Ferry Nice Food takeaway on Ferry Road, a business owned by her daughter.

The flooding on Saturday caused the shop's electrical equipment to go out, their fridges to break, and stock to be lost. It will now be shut for days.

She said: "The damage is devastating. It was very sudden, within 15 to 20 minutes we were knee deep in the water. The banks broke and it was gushing in.

"It's absolutely terrible the barriers weren't used. We've never actually seen them used before and all that money was spent on it. No-one knows yet what happened.

"We know this is a flood area, but we expect help from the council."

She added local businesses were now "rallying together" to help each other, but insurance would not cover them due to them being in a flood area.

Gray said some of the businesses had also requested sandbags ahead of the storm hitting but the council had not provided them.

In 2016, the embankment was described as providing a barrier against direct flooding from the Clyde. It runs westward for 0.62 miles (1km) from Ferry Road.

The pumping station was intended to ensure tidal surges on the Clyde did not cause the Mill Burn to overflow and flood local properties. It was in operation over the weekend.

The flood barriers were being tested and raised when BBC Scotland News was in the area earlier on Monday.

Tarun Wadhwa, who runs the Green Gates Indian Restaurant in Renfrew, was checking the restaurant after closure when he saw the water coming in and rising rapidly.

He said: "It was a disaster. I have never seen the water like that before.

"This will be a big loss for me financially."

He hopes to have the restaurant open again by Tuesday or Wednesday.

A Renfrewshire Council spokesperson said: "The available forecast data and information for the severe weather at the weekend, which included the predicted tide levels for the Clyde, did not meet the currently set threshold for activating the flood barriers in Renfrew.

"Unfortunately, the water levels which affected various locations on the estuary, raised significantly above predicted levels resulting in some local flooding.

"We will review the arrangements in place to ensure these procedures reflect the impacts of a changing climate environment."

Tens of thousands of homes across Scotland remain without power after the storm struck , with wind gusts in some areas of up to 85mph (137km/h).

articles.title: Liam Coen tells Jaguars to ‘leave no doubt’ with penalties
articles.summary: Liam Coen says the Jaguars can’t afford to dwell on questionable officiating, urging his team to stay disciplined and “leave no doubt.”
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have built a reputation as a strong, complete team, but one area has been plaguing them through the entire 2026 season. Penalties have been a constant issue for the Jaguars , but also for the league as a whole.

Through the first four weeks alone , there were 963 accepted penalties, the most through Week 4 since play-by-play data became available in 1978. Week 4 alone featured 271 accepted penalties, the second-most in any week over that span.

The debate over officiating was reignited in Week 7 after several controversial calls in the Detroit Lions ' 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers. Green Bay players openly criticized the officiating afterward, while head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged there were "some tough calls," though ultimately admitted his team had to "play above it."

The conversation surrounding officiating has not been limited to frustrated players and coaches. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed the increase in penalties last week, arguing that the number of flags alone should not be viewed as a reflection of officiating quality.

Asked Monday how he keeps the Jaguars from getting drawn into similar frustration, Coen offered a similar philosophy. "Leave no doubt is really what it comes down to," Coen said. "You know, play above it. Leave no doubt."

Jacksonville has had plenty of experience with the league's flag-heavy start. The Jaguars were penalized 13 times for 125 yards against Cincinnati, and another 13 times for 100 yards against Philadelphia. They were able to improve to just six penalties for 66 yards against Houston, but the timing of several proved costly.

A holding call on Brenton Strange erased a Bhayshul Tuten touchdown against the Texans. Jacksonville was also flagged for having too many players on the field after appearing to force Houston into a third-quarter punt, extending a drive that eventually ended in a touchdown.

Not every call has been without controversy, but Coen's message is that debating which flags were justified does little to help the Jaguars avoid the next one.

"Regardless of results, the fundamentals and techniques in which we coach, teach, we got to continue to detail those even when fatigue sets in and whether it's mental or physical fatigue sets in," Coen said. "We have got to be at our best in terms of detail, fundamentally sharp, disciplined in order to leave no doubt that we control our destiny."

Coen acknowledged that ignoring questionable officiating can be easier said than done. "It's hard not to," he said. "It's human instinct and nature to do so. But it really doesn't do anybody any good to go down that path. Trust me, I've been there."
